relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with LAD type-1 ("This study presents a case of AM in a 5-year-old boy with LAD type-1"); no ITGB2 variant is printed.
method_note: Hand-extracted; no tables in the paper. No ITGB2/CD18 variant is described for the patient (only a general statement that LAD-1 is 'caused by mutations in the CD18 gene'), so no variant rows. The older sibling ('alongside a similar diagnosis in an older sibling') is included as an affected relative with sex not stated, labelled 'sibling of patient'; the diagnosis is only 'similar'. One previously published LAD-I patient from the Discussion is included as 'ref (20) patient' because an individual-level feature (malignant otitis externa) and treatment (simple mastoidectomy) are given; reference (20) in the printed list is a neutropenia paper, so the in-text citation numbering may not match the list. Other literature mentions (Israel cohort of 18, reviews, neutropenia/CGD/hypogammaglobulinemia/cystic fibrosis cases) are group-level or not LAD-I and get no rows. 'on the seventh postnatal day' could modify either the diagnosis or the omphalitis/cord separation, so age at diagnosis and feature onset are left not reported. Age at last evaluation recorded as the stated age at admission ('5-year-old'); later follow-up ages (2 months, 1 year after surgery) are given only relative to surgery. Vital status left not reported (follow-up visits imply but do not state it). Patient was afebrile at admission but later developed persistent fever; only the observed fever is recorded (temporal, not a contradiction). Seropurulent secretion was seen in the ear canal but no purulent discharge at the incision site; checklist 'absence of pus formation' left not reported. Bacteremia (Klebsiella oxytoca in blood cultures) not mapped to checklist 'sepsis'; soft-tissue inflammation around the mastoid not mapped to 'skin or soft tissue infections'. 'Delayed wound healing' excluded is mapped to checklist 'impaired wound healing' (excluded). Leukocytosis based on 'elevated white blood cell and CRP levels' and WBC 41.45 × 109/L.
